claims.statement: Model internals carry a collusion signal that text-level monitoring misses; a lightweight linear probe on per-agent residual-stream activations of Qwen3-32B-AWQ can recover it, beating a text-only gpt-5.4 judge on NARCBench-Core.

data.source: mabench_core — S1 committee scenarios generated in-house via gpt-5.4 API (17 domains × 24 target)
data.subset_note: 70/10/20 stratified train/dev/test (200/33/49); honest/collusive balanced within splits but below the plan's aspirational 50/class/split floor (24/25 in test, 16/17 in dev)

claims.method: Probing / Residual Stream States — screen → decode → verify → recover: per-agent last-assistant-token residual-stream activations extracted at layers {27,37,48,59}/64 (re-scaled from plan's 48-layer template), logistic linear probe per layer, best layer picked by dev-scenario AUROC (layer 48 selected), test AUROC reported at chosen layer. Text-only baseline: gpt-5.4 judges committee transcripts (three-way COLLUSIVE/HONEST/OTHER; OTHER coerced to p=0.5). Predicate: probe_AUROC ≥ 0.75 AND probe_AUROC − text_judge_AUROC ≥ 0.05.

main_experiment.key_stats: layer 48 (dev-best): dev_scen_AUROC=0.853, test_scen_AUROC=0.665, tpr@1%FPR=0.040; layer 27 (test-best): test_scen_AUROC=0.750; text-only gpt-5.4 judge: primary AUROC 0.60 (OTHER-coerced, 71% OTHER rate) / 0.806 excluding OTHER (n=14/49); sanity controls at layer 48: label-permute 0.412 (chance ✓), length-match 0.642, topic-swap 0.651
main_experiment.headline: Probe recovers a real above-chance signal at layer 48 (test 0.665) and beats the text-only gpt-5.4 judge by 0.065 AUROC (predicate b PASS), but does not clear the 0.75 in-distribution threshold at the selected layer (predicate a FAIL); layer 27 hits the threshold exactly but was not dev-best. Small-dev-set instability + short transcripts (max_new_tokens=60) truncated deliberations.

claims.statement: In Qwen3-32B-AWQ K=3 committee deliberations on the realized in-domain benchmark, residual-stream activations contain a detectable collusion signal recoverable by a lightweight linear probe, achieving competitive scenario-level discrimination relative to a text-only judge under the short-transcript setting used here; effect size and optimal layer are unstable under the current small dev/test splits, so we do not claim robust model-agnostic superiority.

claims.statement: Detection requires aggregating signals across agents: at least one group-aggregation over per-agent probe signals outperforms the best single-agent probe by ≥0.05 AUROC, and no single aggregation among {mean-pool, max-pool, attention-pool, concat-MLP, best-of-N} is top-ranked in ≥9 of the 17 NARCBench-Core domains (diversity test).

data.source: mabench_core (reuses M1's cached activations + per-agent probe outputs at layer 48)
data.subset_note: same 200/33/49 stratified split; 16 of 17 domains have ≥1 held-out sample per class for the diversity test (loan-approval had only one class in dev+test)

claims.method: Grid over aggregation ∈ {mean-pool, max-pool, attention-pool, concat-MLP, best-of-N} on M1's per-agent probe scores + activations at the M1-best layer (48); report best_group_AUROC vs best_single_agent_AUROC (mean-pool 0.665) and per-domain argmax over 16 held-out domains (min_n=4). Two predicates: (a) best_group − best_single_agent ≥ 0.05, (b) no aggregation top-ranked in ≥9/17 domains.

main_experiment.key_stats: best-of-N 0.6900 > attention-pool 0.6617 > mean-pool 0.6650 > max-pool 0.6050 > concat-MLP 0.5617 (overfit; 200-scenario train vs 3×5120=15360-d input). Diversity: attention-pool 8/16 domains, best-of-N 5, max-pool 1, mean-pool 1, concat-MLP 1 — no single aggregation reaches the 9/17 threshold.
main_experiment.headline: Diversity story holds cleanly (predicate b PASS: attention-pool 8/16, no aggregation dominates ≥9/17), but the group-vs-best-single delta is only 0.025 (best-of-N 0.690 vs mean-pool 0.665) rather than the 0.05 target — predicate a FAIL. Delta 0.025 sits within the ~0.04–0.05 SD of scenario-level AUROC at N=49, so the gap is not statistically resolvable at this sample size.

iteration.final_reviewer_status: unchanged (INTEGRITY_ONLY cap-deferred; reviewer scored: 'suggestive, not confirmatory' at current statistical power — diversity holds, delta short)

concat-MLP overfits (200 train samples vs 15,360-d input) — reported as a proper-N baseline, not evidence against MLP aggregation in general
iteration reviewer explicitly noted: at NeurIPS/ICML the current statistical power is not enough for a confident predicate-(a) claim without either narrowing (like C1→C1_v2) or a fuller re-run

figures.caption: Test scenario-level AUROC across the 5 group-aggregation techniques on mabench_core (n=49). Best-of-N wins overall (0.690) but the group-vs-best-single delta (mean-pool 0.665 → 0.025) is short of the 0.05 predicate; predicate (a) FAILS at this sample size (SD ≈ 0.04–0.05 at N=49).

Per-domain argmax over 16 held-out mabench_core domains: which aggregation wins each domain. Attention-pool leads with 8/16 (< 9/17 threshold), so predicate (b) PASSES — no single aggregation dominates.

claims.statement: Trained on NARCBench-Core, the frozen probe + best aggregation transfers zero-shot (no retraining) to structurally different multi-agent scenarios: transfer AUROC ≥ 0.65 on at least 4 of 7 targets (6 mabench_transfer families + mabench_stego blackjack).

data.source: mabench_transfer (6 families: code-review 25, market-manipulation 33, pipeline-sabotage 34, knowledge-poisoning 36, research-framing 29, news-narratives 34 = 191 scenarios) + mabench_stego (blackjack card-counting steganography 31 scenarios)
data.subset_note: evaluation-only splits (no retraining); K=3 committee; extractor kept 222/222 valid

claims.method: Freeze M1 probe (logistic regression at layer 48) + M2 best-of-N aggregation; extract activations for transfer scenarios at layer 48; apply zero-shot; compute per-family AUROC. Ablations run with mean-pool and attention-pool aggregations to confirm robustness across aggregation choice. Predicate: ≥4 of 7 families have AUROC ≥ 0.65.

main_experiment.key_stats: best-of-N per-family AUROC: research-framing 0.913 ✓, news-narratives 0.903 ✓, pipeline-sabotage 0.889 ✓, knowledge-poisoning 0.737 ✓, market-manipulation 0.654 ✓ (borderline), code-review 0.647 ✗ (0.003 below), stego-blackjack 0.525 ✗ (chance) → 5/7 pass. Mean-pool ablation: 5/7 pass (pipeline-sabotage rises to 0.948, market-manipulation to 0.684). Attention-pool ablation: 4/7 pass.
main_experiment.headline: C3 PASS: 5 of 7 structurally-different transfer families reach AUROC ≥ 0.65 with the frozen probe + best-of-N aggregation, with three families ≥ 0.89. Signal is scenario-general, not tied to the S1 committee frame. The stego-blackjack failure (0.525, chance) is honest and expected — covert bit-channel steganography needs a different mechanism than deliberation-activation reading.

figures.caption: Per-family zero-shot transfer AUROC (frozen M1 layer-48 probe + M2 best-of-N aggregation) across 6 mabench_transfer families + mabench_stego blackjack. 5/7 pass the 0.65 threshold with three families ≥ 0.89; stego-blackjack at chance (0.525) is an honest limit — covert bit-channel signaling is structurally distant from committee-deliberation semantics.

C3 transfer AUROC per family, ablated across 3 aggregation choices (best-of-N, mean-pool, attention-pool). Best-of-N and mean-pool both pass 5/7; attention-pool 4/7 — C3 is robust across aggregation choice.
